metadata.title: Charak Samhita - Indriya Sthana & Chikitsa Sthana
metadata.description: Comprehensive Ayurvedic knowledge from Charak Samhita covering sensorial prognosis (Indriya Sthana) and therapeutic principles (Chikitsa Sthana)

sthanas.description: Indriya Sthana deals with the observation of signs predicting lifespan and signs indicative of reduced duration of remaining life (also called arishta lakshana). The word Indriya literally means organ, sense, force, vigor. In the present context, it means prana or vital life force. The seat of prana in the body is sneha or ojas. Indriya (sense organs) are said to be the linga (organs) of prana.

chapters.englishName: Fatal signs in complexion and voice
chapters.summary: The chapter Varnasvariyam Indriyam Adhyaya is about arishta lakshana (near death signs) perceived by auditory and visual senses. Swara (Voice) is an audible feature, whereas color and complexion are visual features. Sudden change in frequency, rhythm, resonance, tone, the pitch of voice and complexion of the body is indicative of serious pathology of the body. Charak has placed Indriya Sthana (section about near death signs) before Chikitsa Sthana (section about the treatment of diseases) possibly, to guide physician when not to treat a patient.
keyConcepts: Lakshana Nimitta - Caused by bodily marks
Lakshya Nimitta - Caused by etiological factors
Nimitta Anuroopa Vikriti - Breakdown for no apparent reason
Abnormal complexion - Blue, blackish, coppery, green, snow white
importantVerses: Normal complexion in one half and abnormal in other half indicates death
Sudden appearance of abnormal complexion without cause indicates death
Abnormal voice changes indicate grave prognosis
Knowledge of these facts helps in knowing patient's lifespan

chapters.englishName: Fatal signs of Tactile and Olfactory perception
chapters.summary: This chapter sums up the variations in the sense of taste of the body and smell of the individual which indicate imminent death of the person (Arishta Lakshana). Variations in the smell of body and the altered taste sense of a person may reveal the disease processes in that patient. After describing fatal signs regarding complexion and voice, diagnosed by visual and auditory senses respectively, the present chapter describes signs to be examined by gustatory and olfactory senses.
importantVerses: Person emitting flower fragrance day and night will die within a year
Person with various repulsive odors is also pushpita
Person stinking with perfumed ointment indicates death
Pleasant or unpleasant smell continuously without cause - death within year

chapters.englishName: Palpable signs of Imminent Death
chapters.summary: Parimarshaneeyam Indriyam Adhyaya deals with signs and symptoms of imminent death; especially the ones which can be elicited by touch or palpation. The chapter talks about various changes that occur in different parts of the body along with various signs elicited by palpation like hardening, softening, bowing, displacement of body structures, changes in breathing patterns, extreme wasting along with deficiency of blood, structural and functional changes in eyes, body hair, and various body parts.
importantVerses: If feet, calves, thighs are cold, stiff, insensitive, inflexible - person is nearing death
Ankles, knees, pelvis displaced from normal position indicates death soon
Signs without causative factors indicate imminent death

chapters.englishName: Fatal signs in five sense organs
chapters.summary: This chapter explicates about the alterations in the perception of the five sense organs which reveal impending death of an individual. The previous three chapters described arishta lakhana as perceived by senses vision, sound, taste and touch. This chapter describes arishta lakhana as perceived by all five Indriya or senses. Indriya and aneekam indicate the group of all five sense organs. There is a good synchronization between all sense organs for conversion of information into the knowledge.
importantVerses: Alterations in perception of five sense organs reveal impending death
Synchronization between sense organs important for knowledge conversion
Abnormal sensory perceptions indicate specific underlying morbidity

chapters.englishName: Predicting prognosis of diseases by prodromal symptoms
chapters.summary: Purvarupeeyam Indriyam Adhyaya has been devoted to predict prognosis of diseases by prodromal symptoms. This chapter suggests that knowledge and examination of prodromal symptoms was important in ancient times and emphasis was given that physician should carefully recognize disease in early stage and predict course of disease. Various aspects of dreams including physiology, types, interpretation and prognostic importance have also been described.
importantVerses: If all prodromal symptoms are manifesting and severe, condition will be fatal
Prodromal symptoms converting to particular disease can be termed prognostic sign
Dreams should be analyzed before predicting prognosis

chapters.englishName: Specific fatal clinical features
chapters.summary: This chapter, Katamanisharireeyam Indriyam Adhyaya, explains some specific clinical features that are different than sensory perceptions and prodromal symptoms. Most of the time they indicate serious complications and are indicative of imminent death. This chapter is a random compilation of bad prognostic features of diseases that are mentioned in Nidana Sthana and Chikitsa Sthana.
keyConcepts: Katamani Sharireeyam - Types of disease presentations
importantVerses: Severe chest pain with vomiting and inability to digest is incurable
Gambheera hikka with bleeding diarrhea should not be given medication
Diarrhea with anaha and trishna in weak person - dangerous
Emaciated person with diminished strength and fainting succumbs to death immediately

chapters.englishName: Fatal signs of changes in shadows, complexion, and luster
chapters.summary: The seventh chapter Pannarupiyam Indriyam Adhyaya deals with the loss of shadow image in eyes, changes in complexion and luster indicative of imminent death. Difference between shadow and luster is also explained in this chapter with characteristic features of shadows pertaining to each of pancha mahabhuta.
importantVerses: Distortion in image reflected in pupil indicates imminent death
Any deformity in shadow in moonlight, sunlight, lamp, water, mirror - considered dead
Distortion in shape, measurement, color, luster is ominous even in healthy
Bright things looking dull indicates impending death

chapters.englishName: Fatal signs like inverted shadow of dying person
chapters.summary: In this chapter, thirty six moribund signs starting with avakshira, i.e. inverted shadow of the dying person are described. These moribund signs can be classified into physical and emotional-spiritual-psychological types. The changes in eyelids, eyebrows, face, scalp, nose, tongue, ears, and in abnormal movements of body are described to indicate declining lifespan and death.
importantVerses: Shadow inverted, distorted or without head - do not treat
Eye-lashes matted, sight fixed - do not treat
Eyelids swollen, not meeting, eyes smeared - regard as dead
Hair appearing as if anointed though not - end of life

chapters.englishName: Signs and Symptoms useful for Palliative Care among Patients approaching Death
chapters.summary: This chapter includes various signs and symptoms related to imminent death that start with changes in color of eyes and identified in a patient as well as in healthy individuals. It has been emphasized that physician should have knowledge of all Arishta Lakshana described in this chapter. Description of eight grave diseases and symptoms of approaching death are important topics which add value to this chapter. These signs are important in palliative care.
importantVerses: All Arishta Lakshana should be known to physician
Only few manifest at a time - proper examination needed
Features indicating grave prognosis when associated with disease
Physician should identify features of impending death

chapters.englishName: Signs of instant death and incurable complications of several diseases
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with incurable complications of several diseases which can lead to a patient to an instantaneous death. It enlists some emergency conditions for intensive care. The many signs and symptoms listed in this chapter are manageable now by advanced medical and surgical techniques.
importantVerses: Patient with painful vata shthila in cardiac region with intense thirst dies instantly
Patient with kapha in throat blocking breathing dies
Physician who comprehends signs can anticipate survival or death

chapters.englishName: Signs and Symptoms of Imminent Death caused due to diminution of Agni
chapters.summary: This chapter explicates the signs and symptoms of imminent death due to diminution of Agni (factor responsible for digestion and metabolism). The components of life like lifespan, strength, complexion, enthusiasm, health, growth, luster, and immunity are dependent upon the status of agni.
importantVerses: Person with poor digestion, unstable mind, diminished luster, weak mental strength dies within year
Six attributes changes indicate death within six months
Signs originated due to extensively vitiated dosha transcending treatment stage are called arishta

chapters.englishName: Auspicious and Inauspicious Characteristics of the messenger
chapters.summary: The concluding chapter is about auspicious and inauspicious features of the informer, or the person who wants to take the physician to the house of the patient. There is a description of his physical appearance, mental status, behavior, time of calling, the circumstances while on the way to the patient's house, condition of patient's house, surroundings, family members, availability of requirements for treatment.
importantVerses: Inauspicious signs in messenger indicate patient is incurable
Late night arrival - inauspicious for patient's life
House being cleaned when physician arrives - seriously inauspicious
Departing auspicious articles indicate departing life of patient

sthanas.description: Chikitsa Sthana deals with therapeutic principles and treatment of various diseases. It contains 30 chapters covering rejuvenation therapy, aphrodisiacs, fever management, bleeding disorders, tumors, diabetes, skin diseases, tuberculosis, mental disorders, epilepsy, and many more conditions.

chapters.englishName: Rejuvenation therapy
chapters.summary: Rasayana, the first chapter of the Chikitsa Sthana deals with one of the most important specialties of Ashtanga Ayurveda, namely, Rasayana Tantra. Rasayana means rejuvenation and anti-ageing therapies in Ayurveda. It also includes all measures for geriatric healthcare and immunity enhancement. This chapter is divided in four padas dealing with different aspects of Rasayana therapy.

chapters.englishName: Aphrodisiac therapy, virility and treatment of sexual dysfunctions
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Vajikarana - the science of aphrodisiacs and sexual health. It describes various formulations and therapies for improving virility, treating sexual dysfunctions, and enhancing reproductive capacity. The chapter covers both psychological and physical aspects of sexual health.

chapters.englishName: Management of Jwara (different types of fever)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with the management of Jwara - fever. It describes various types of fever, their causes, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, and treatment approaches. The chapter covers both acute and chronic fever conditions with detailed therapeutic protocols.

chapters.englishName: Management of Raktapitta (Bleeding Disorders)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Raktapitta - bleeding disorders. It covers conditions involving abnormal bleeding from various parts of the body. The chapter describes the pathophysiology, types, clinical features, and management strategies for various bleeding disorders.

chapters.englishName: Management of Gulma
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Gulma - abdominal tumors and swellings. It describes various types of gulma, their etiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and treatment approaches including both conservative and surgical management.

chapters.englishName: Management of Prameha (Urinary Diseases including diabetes)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Prameha - urinary disorders including diabetes. It describes the types of prameha, their causes, pathophysiology, clinical features, and comprehensive management including diet, lifestyle, and therapeutic interventions.

chapters.englishName: Management of Kushtha (Skin Diseases)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Kushtha - skin diseases including leprosy. It describes eighteen types of Kushtha, their etiology, clinical features, and comprehensive treatment approaches including external applications, internal medications, and purification therapies.

chapters.englishName: Management of Rajayakshma (Wasting Diseases/Tuberculosis)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Rajayakshma - wasting diseases and tuberculosis. It describes the etiology, pathophysiology, clinical features, and comprehensive management including nutritional support, therapeutic interventions, and lifestyle modifications.

chapters.englishName: Management of Unmada (Psychosis/Mental Disorders)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Unmada - mental disorders and psychosis. It describes various types of mental illnesses, their causes, clinical presentation, and treatment approaches including psychotherapy, medications, and lifestyle modifications.

chapters.englishName: Management of Apasmara (Seizure/Epilepsy)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Apasmara - epilepsy and seizure disorders. It describes the types, causes, clinical presentation, and management strategies for epilepsy including dietary modifications, herbal treatments, and lifestyle changes.

chapters.englishName: Management of Kshata-kshina (Emaciation due to Trauma)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Kshata-kshina - emaciation due to trauma and physical injuries. It describes the management of chest injuries, wounds, and cachexia resulting from trauma or excessive physical exertion.

chapters.englishName: Management of Shvayathu (Various types of Swellings)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Shvayathu - various types of swellings and edematous conditions. It describes the etiology, types, clinical presentation, and treatment approaches for different kinds of swellings.

chapters.englishName: Management of Udara (Generalized enlargement of Abdomen)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Udara - generalized abdominal enlargement including ascites, hepatomegaly, and splenomegaly. It describes the causes, clinical features, and treatment approaches for these conditions.

chapters.englishName: Management of Arsha (Hemorrhoids)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Arsha - hemorrhoids. It describes the types, causes, clinical presentation, and treatment approaches including both conservative management and surgical interventions.

chapters.englishName: Management of Grahani (Diseases of digestion and metabolism)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Grahani - disorders of digestion and metabolism. It describes conditions affecting the digestive system and metabolic processes with their management approaches.

chapters.englishName: Management of Pandu (Anemia and diseases due to blood deficiency)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Pandu - anemia and blood deficiency disorders. It also covers Kamala (jaundice and hepatic disorders) as they are caused mainly by vitiation of rakta (blood tissue).

chapters.englishName: Management of Hikka (Hiccups) and Shwasa (Dyspnea)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Hikka (hiccups) and Shwasa (dyspnea/breathing difficulties). It describes five types of hiccups and various respiratory disorders with their management approaches.

chapters.englishName: Management of Kasa (Cough of various origins)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Kasa - cough of various origins. It describes different types of cough, their causes, clinical presentation, and treatment approaches.

chapters.englishName: Management of Atisara (Diarrhea and associated disorders)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Atisara - diarrhea and associated disorders. It describes various types of diarrhea, their causes, clinical presentation, and management approaches including diet and lifestyle modifications.

chapters.englishName: Management of Chhardi (Vomiting)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Chhardi - vomiting. It describes the causes, types, clinical presentation, and management strategies for vomiting disorders.

chapters.englishName: Management of Visarpa (Acute spreading erysepalas)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Visarpa - acute inflammatory skin conditions like erysipelas. It describes the clinical features and treatment approaches for these acute spreading dermatological conditions.

chapters.englishName: Management of Trishna (Morbid thirst)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Trishna - morbid thirst. It describes the causes, clinical presentation, and management approaches for conditions manifesting as excessive thirst.

chapters.englishName: Management of Visha (Various types of poisoning)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Visha - various types of poisoning including toxicology and detoxification. It describes the management of different poisoning cases with appropriate therapeutic interventions.

chapters.englishName: Management of Madatyaya (Intoxication/Alcoholism)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Madatyaya - intoxication and alcoholism. It describes the management of acute and chronic stages of alcoholic intoxication and its complications.

chapters.englishName: Management of two types of Vrana (Ulcers)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Vrana - ulcers and wound management. It describes two types of ulcers and their management including surgical procedures and conservative treatments.

chapters.englishName: Management of Trimarma (Diseases of three vital organs)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Trimarma - diseases affecting three vital organs (heart, brain, and pelvis). It describes the management of conditions affecting these critical anatomical regions.

chapters.englishName: Management of Urustambha (Diseases of thigh and hip)
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Urustambha - disorders affecting the thigh and hip region including degenerative conditions. It describes the clinical features and treatment approaches.

chapters.englishName: Management of diseases caused by vata dosha
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Vatavyadhi - disorders caused by vata dosha. It describes the various neurological and musculoskeletal conditions resulting from vata imbalance and their management.

chapters.englishName: Management of diseases involving vata and rakta
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Vatarakta - disorders involving vata and rakta (blood). It describes conditions where both vata and blood are affected with their management approaches.

chapters.englishName: Management of disorders of genital tract
chapters.summary: This chapter deals with Yonivyapat - disorders of the female genital tract. It describes various gynecological conditions and their management including reproductive health issues.
